questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Seeing something new, cheap location, easy access to accommodation

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The coordinator was really good at telling us what to expect prior to arrival. I also found it very helpful that the university suggested accommodation in Riga.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had introduction days when we arrived. This helped us get close together in the Erasmus group.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: As soon as you have confirmation that you will go to the host institution, find accommodation. It makes the process of going much calmer. One of my friends did not have accommodation when he arrived, and it made his first period in Riga very stressful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Writing an e-mail to the administration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration was very helpful and always answered quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Always succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is easy and just ask the administration!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had mostly BA courses but also one MA. The academic level was ok, but the local students were not very good. It is easy to be an exchange student from the university, but I do not think it is easy to be an exchange student from the university. I liked that it was not only the exam that counted but also the participation. It made sure that I showed up to class and was an active part of the class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More informal. It was like being in high school and the teachers always knew your name.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economic diplomacy, law of state responsibility, environmental law, political negotiations, tactics and style, global approaches to public diplomacy, International Human Rights Institutions, Procedures and Mechanisms, International Humanitarian law, Legal Aspects of the External Relations of EU, Geo-economics: the Geopolitics of Energy, International Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global approaches and Geo-economics! The teachers are amazing. Political negotiation is really fun if you like debating.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: travels with my new friends. In general I spend a lot of money on having fun with friends, so it is possible to live cheaper than me in Riga.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were fun parties in the school. There were other opportunities, but the local students were acting very young and it felt a bit like high school, so personally I did not go.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The parties.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Estonia, Poland and Lithuania. It is all easily accessible from Riga. A day trip to Sigulda or Gauja national park is also fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes and no. The exchange community is strong, but the Latvians are not very social.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Give it time. They will eventually work with you when they see that you do good academically.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The lack of spontaneity and need for structure. The Latvians we met often had a hard time adjusting to new things. They were sweet when you got them to talk, but if you did anything they weren't uses to they would get mad.  
The roads were very slippery and the city did nothing. Also the emergency room was closed on the weekends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The karaoke bar was fun. Everything was cheap and that was also nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The local students are academically not very good unfortunately. 
2. It is easy to get good grades. 
3. You have to be active in class.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Focus on the friends you meet in school.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from all over Europe. Learning new things about cultures and sharing my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The slippery roads of Riga and my home university not responding and "losing" my e-mail. My host university was good at responding me, but I felt like I never got any real help from my home uni.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
